Fix staging reminder false positive on -m messages

stages_all() treated any short-option word containing the letter "a"
as git commit -a. For `git commit -m"add export handler"`, shlex yields
the single word `-madd export handler`, whose message text contains
"a", so the reminder fired even though nothing is staged.

Scan short-option clusters letter by letter and stop at a letter that
takes a value (m, F, C, c, t for commit), since the rest of the word is
that value. Add regression cases for the -m message form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

target:
The reminder fired on `git commit -m"add export handler"` because the check for `git commit -a` matched the letter `a` inside the commit message. I fixed it and committed the fix as `7b9d694` on `main`.

**Cause:** `stages_all()` in `src/staging.py` treated any short-option word containing `a` as `-a`. `shlex` turns `-m"add export handler"` into the single word `-madd export handler`, and the `a` in "add" matched.

**Fix:** The scan now walks the option letters one at a time and stops at a letter that takes a value (`m`, `F`, `C`, `c`, `t` for commit), since the rest of that word is the value. `-am` still counts as stage-all, and `-ma "x"` correctly doesn't.

**Tests:** I added `git commit -m"add export handler"` and `git commit -madd-export` to the must-pass list in `tests/test_staging.py`. Both failed before the fix. All 5 tests pass after it.

**Commit:** It touches only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py`, staged by name, with the Haiku co-author line. I left out your uncommitted README note and the untracked `notes/` draft.
